nm_el_rito_sport_area.blurb: El Rito Sport Area sits in the hills above the village of El Rito in northern New Mexico, near 7,600 feet. The rock is conglomerate: rounded cobbles set in a hard matrix, with the cobbles and the holes they leave behind forming the holds, many of them pockets. Walls run from vertical to overhanging, and the routes are almost all bolted sport, with a few boulders and a handful of other lines. Most grades fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common and a few easier lines below. The climbing is concentrated in a tight set of walls such as Beer Block, Rad Wall, Pirate's Wall and El Norte.

sd_cathedral_spires.blurb: The Cathedral Spires are a group of granite pillars in the Needles of Custer State Park, in the Black Hills of South Dakota, set along Needles Highway beyond a hike of about a mile. Five main ridges, numbered one through five, rise out of the gullies, with climbing on every side and some longer multi-pitch routes. Almost everything is traditional, and placing gear is not always straightforward. In the Needles as a whole, quartz crystals make up many of the holds on the spires. Grades range from easy ground to 5.13, with the weight between 5.7 and 5.12. Khayyam Spire, Spire Four and Spire Five are the larger formations.

ak_interior_alaska_alaska_range.blurb: The Alaska Range arcs across south-central Alaska, crowned by Denali, and this grouping spans its glaciated mountains and the Interior. Denali National Park alone holds well over a million acres of glaciers, and many remote glaciers are reached by ski plane. Weather in the range is harsh. Alpine routes lead here, followed by bouldering and ice, with a smaller amount of rock. Ice grades run from moderate to WI6, rock routes mostly 5.8 to 5.11, and boulder problems mostly V0 to V7. The Delta Range, east of the Delta River, is lower than the western range and gets far less traffic than the Denali region, mixing crag, ice and boulder climbing near Bear Creek and Black Rapids.

az_pit_aka_le_petit_verdon_the.blurb: The Pit, also called Le Petit Verdon, is a limestone escarpment just south of Flagstaff, Arizona, near 6,700 feet. The rock is pocketed white Kaibab limestone, and the routes are generally short, well bolted and edgy. The cliff is split into tiers. It is described as pleasant and climbable year-round. Sport climbing is nearly all of it, with a few trad, top-rope and boulder lines. Grades start around 5.7, but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with 5.11 the most common and a solid group of 5.13s, so it is better for people already leading at that level than for beginners. Nose Rock, Way Gone Wall, The Oven, The White Wall and Swiss Tower are the larger crags.

co_rotary_park.blurb: Rotary Park is a bouldering area beside Horsetooth Reservoir, on the west side of Fort Collins, Colorado, with the reservoir to its west and Maxwell Natural Area to its east. It is almost entirely bouldering, plus a few top-rope lines. The problems run from very easy up to V9 and above, with most between V0 and V5, so there is plenty for beginners and for people building up. The boulders are spread along a ridge that faces west, which lets climbers chase sun or shade through the day, and the area is climbed all year. Eliminator Boulder, Mental Block, Meditation Boulder and Pitch Penny Boulder are among the bigger sub-areas.
